title: Exported arrays' data persists between scenes, no garbage collection?
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.4.1.stable.mono.official [49a5bc7b6]

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7640) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900KF (32 threads)

### Issue description

Godot Arrays of any type, be it a custom resource, int, string, etc. if part of a code-instantiated node, will have data that persists between scenes. It should work similar to other collections, such as the basic arrays, where once there's no reference to this data any longer, the data goes into the garbage collection, right?

### Steps to reproduce

Create two scenes. Create a packed scene with a single node with a script. Inside that script, create an array, set it to be exported. Give it several values in the editor. In code, print the values first, then add a few extra values to it (or change the values, or remove values, whatever). Make whatever way you want of getting from scene 1 to scene 2 (such as a key input). Create a script, using it for the base nodes of each scene, which instantiates into the scene the previously mentioned node using an export of a packed scene. See how the data persists. 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[testprojectcsharp4.4.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20446306/testprojectcsharp4.4.zip)
